newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spot down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spot down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Wednesday, consolidating at high levels due to new domestic A share issues, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell slightly to 11.00 percent from 12.00 percent on Tuesday.
Turnover fell to 7.91 million lots from 8.45 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Gansu Tristar Petrochemical (Group) Co issued A shares in Shanghai today, the third new firm making its debut this week. New issues have helped keep the rates at high levels this week.
Traders expect the rates to fall during the rest of this week with no new issues in sight.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Wednesday due to institutional profit-taking after yesterday's gains, traders said.
But the most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 bucked the trend and rose to 123.16 yuan from 122.31 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose slightly to 1.72 million lots from 1.52 million.
Traders expect the spot contracts to consolidate down in the short term. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
